results.evidence: Real contradiction: beta and pitch_detail describe a brushy west-side approach over Gray Wolf Ridge from Baldy, the approach/waypoints/approach_variants describe the Royal Basin traverse to an east/southeast gully (while calling it the 'West Side'), and itinerary day 2 describes a ridge crest reached from the north. Web research was cut off by a tool session limit before the standard summit line could be established from two sources, so nothing was changed.

The park's Royal Basin page gives the climb to Royal Lake as 2,550 to 5,100 ft, i.e. a trailhead near 2,550 ft, which fits the row's own '~2,500 ft gain' to the lake and contradicts the 2,960-2,970 ft stated for the trailhead. A second independent source could not be fetched (tool session limit), and the WTA page does not state the trailhead elevation, so the waypoint elev and approach prose were left unchanged.

Official park pages disagree: the Royal Basin trip page gives the quota season as May 1-September 30, while the park's wilderness-reservations page says the summer online season is May 15-October 15. A search summary also gave June 15-October 15. With no two sources agreeing, no field was changed. (bivy[1].permit is owned by the camping clean-up and was not touched.)

results.correct_value: Camp only in the designated sites at Royal Creek, Lower Royal Meadow or Royal Lake; no camping in Upper Royal Basin
results.evidence: The park's own Royal Basin trip page lists the designated camping areas as Royal Creek, Lower Royal Meadow and Royal Lake, says to camp in designated sites only and states there is no camping in Upper Royal Basin; it gives Royal Lake as 7.2 mi and 2,550 to 5,100 ft. WTA's Royal Basin hike page independently says camping is permitted only at designated sites at Royal Lake, with Upper Royal Basin (5,700 ft) about three-quarters of a mile beyond. A third hiking page describes the upper basin as day-use. The camp is therefore Royal Lake; day gains/losses were shifted between days so the itinerary totals still equal gain_ft/loss_ft. bivy[0] (Upper Royal Basin, role main) also presents the upper basin as a camp but belongs to the camping clean-up, so it was not patched.

results.evidence: The park's Royal Basin page names the Upper Dungeness Trailhead as a USFS trailhead and says the parking pass required is a Northwest Forest Pass or America the Beautiful pass. The park's wilderness-reservations page gives the camping fees ($8 per person per night for ages 16+, $6 reservation fee). The access fields that asked for a $30 entrance pass were corrected.
